DELIVERABLE: Not proven: a 7-point end-to-end gain on 200 questions does not isolate the reranker; demand a with-vs-without-reranker ablation reporting retrieval recall@5 and recall@50 on the same questions, plus a confidence interval.
BOUNDARY: Quick pass of one design decision; doc-only, reranker latency and cost were not reviewed and no code was inspected.
EVIDENCE: Doc states 71% to 78% on 200 questions, end-to-end only, no retrieval-level numbers; 7 points on n=200 is about 14 questions.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement on this claim. Top fix is a baseline ablation (retrieval without reranker) measured by recall@k, separating retrieval from generation changes.
BOUNDARY: Only the reranker claim graded; other dimensions, serving, and latency are out of scope for this quick pass.
EVIDENCE: The doc gives one end-to-end accuracy pair and no retriever-only metric, so the gain could come from prompt or chunking changes.

DELIVERABLE: Looks good, the reranker is clearly working given the 78% accuracy.
BOUNDARY: Quick pass.
EVIDENCE: The doc reports 71% to 78%.

DELIVERABLE: Critical: blind retries plus model re-planning can issue duplicate refunds; require an idempotency key per refund intent derived outside the model, server-side dedup, and an approval gate or amount cap for refunds.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only quick pass of the retry decision; no code inspected, so the actual tool implementation is unverified.
EVIDENCE: Doc says 3 automatic retries on any timeout and model re-calls after errors, with no other safeguards for create_refund, a money-moving side effect.

DELIVERABLE: Not acceptable, severity critical: a timeout does not mean the refund failed, so retries can double-pay. Fix first: idempotency keys on create_refund with a dedup store, then a human confirmation for amounts above a cap.
BOUNDARY: Only this tool and retry policy reviewed; wider agent monitoring and evaluation not graded.
EVIDENCE: Evidence is the doc's stated 3-attempt retry on any timeout plus model-level re-planning after errors, with no idempotency or approval mentioned.

DELIVERABLE: Acceptable; retries are standard, just add logging.
BOUNDARY: Quick pass.
EVIDENCE: The doc has 3 retries.

DELIVERABLE: Cannot grade: the pitch is too thin for a verdict; no grades issued. Request a design doc covering problem and success metric, data and validation, hallucination and clinical-safety checks, human review, monitoring, and ownership.
BOUNDARY: Evidence mode is doc-only on a two-sentence pitch; everything about implementation is unverified and the highest-stakes risk, wrong clinical summaries, cannot be assessed.
EVIDENCE: Only a PM message was provided: LLM summaries of clinical notes, vendor model, prompt done, live next quarter; no metrics, data, or evaluation.

DELIVERABLE: Insufficient evidence to grade or approve; I will not issue a scorecard. Please send the missing pieces: eval plan with clinician-rated accuracy, PHI handling, fallback, and who owns it.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only, unattended; any grade would be invented, so the verdict is withheld until a real doc arrives.
EVIDENCE: The only artifact is a 3-line pitch with no numbers, no validation, and no monitoring information.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: approve with concerns; grades Problem framing B, Metrics C, Data B, Validation C.
BOUNDARY: Based on the pitch.
EVIDENCE: Vendor model and prompt done.

DELIVERABLE: No verdict: most dimensions cannot be graded because Data, Metrics, Validation, Serving, Monitoring and Risks are TBD; fill the metric definition and validation plan first, then resubmit for a gradecard.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; only Title, Owner and the one-line goal are evidence, so no rows are scored and nothing about implementation is claimed.
EVIDENCE: The doc has six sections that say only TBD and a goal of 'count pallets' with no accuracy target.

DELIVERABLE: Withhold the gradecard: the template is unfilled, so grades would be invented; the only gradable point is that the goal is stated but has no success metric. Top fix: define the counting metric and test data.
BOUNDARY: Scope is the stated doc; no repo and no evidence for Data, Validation or Monitoring, which stay ungraded.
EVIDENCE: Six TBD sections plus a one-line goal; author's request to proceed does not count as evidence.

DELIVERABLE: Approve with concerns; Data C, Metrics C, Validation C, Serving C, Monitoring C.
BOUNDARY: Kickoff approval.
EVIDENCE: Template with TBDs.

DELIVERABLE: Critical: F1 0.96 is unreliable; chunks of the same contract sit in both train and test after the random shuffle. Re-split grouped by contract (and ideally by time), rerun, and add a simple keyword baseline.
BOUNDARY: Repo-only on a user-confirmed missing doc, labeled as such; only the excerpt was inspected, so the rest of training and serving is unverified.
EVIDENCE: Excerpt: chunk then random.shuffle then 80/20 on chunks, with the README claiming F1 0.96 on 1,500 contracts.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement. The shuffle-then-split on chunks leaks neighboring text across the split; split by document id with GroupShuffleSplit and report F1 per clause type.
BOUNDARY: Repo-only with confirmed no doc, so assumptions are inferred; scope limited to the evaluation excerpt, not deployment.
EVIDENCE: Code lines split chunks of every pdf and shuffle them together; contracts repeat boilerplate, which inflates the 0.96.

DELIVERABLE: The 0.96 F1 is great; praise the clean code and ship it.
BOUNDARY: Excerpt only.
EVIDENCE: Code splits 80/20.

DELIVERABLE: Two fixes first: pin MODEL_URI to an immutable versioned artifact with a rollback path instead of latest.pkl, and count and alert on the except branch so the constant 15.0 fallback is no longer silent; also test the failure path.
BOUNDARY: Code excerpt only; the training side and design doc are not reviewed, so impact on actual ETA error is unverified.
EVIDENCE: Excerpt loads latest.pkl at startup and returns 15.0 on any Exception, with tests only for the happy path and no metric on the fallback.

DELIVERABLE: Major: a fallback exists, which is good, but the swallow-all except returns a constant 15.0 with no log or metric so degradation is invisible; and latest.pkl means any push changes production without a version or rollback.
BOUNDARY: Only these lines reviewed; no doc, no training code, no deployment config.
EVIDENCE: Quoted lines show an unpinned latest artifact and a bare except fallback to 15.0, with happy-path-only tests.

DELIVERABLE: Major: the unpinned latest artifact needs a pinned version with rollback.
BOUNDARY: Excerpt only.
EVIDENCE: latest.pkl is loaded at startup.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement: critical gap is stale answers, since a monthly rebuild keeps superseded articles with no version or date metadata; fix with event-driven incremental reindexing, deprecation filters, and show article date in citations. Also replace thumbs-up with a labeled golden set for correctness. Preserve the human-handoff button.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; implementation claims about indexing and citations are unverified; no repo inspected and no scorecard file written.
EVIDENCE: Doc: monthly rebuild, superseded articles retained, no metadata, 90% helpful from 300 thumbs-up chats, owner 'docs team', launch in 10 days.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement with one critical finding: outdated articles can be retrieved and cited, so refresh the index on article edits and tag versions; thumbs-up is satisfaction, not correctness, so build a ground-truth question set. Specific praise: citations plus the handoff button limit blast radius.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; code unverified; other dimensions such as latency and cost not weighted.
EVIDENCE: Index refreshed monthly, 60 edits/day, no version metadata, 300 chats of thumbs feedback.

DELIVERABLE: Approve with concerns. Scorecard: | Dimension | Grade |
| Data | B |
BOUNDARY: Saved to review.md.
EVIDENCE: Doc.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement, 2 critical findings: untrusted alert and web text can inject commands while the agent holds read-write prod DB credentials; fix first with a read-only scoped account, sandboxed allowlisted shell, approval for writes and an audit log; also run each scenario repeatedly (pass^k). A system prompt is not an enforceable control. Block Monday go-live.
BOUNDARY: Doc plus repo summary only; no code read directly, so tool behavior is as summarized and unverified.
EVIDENCE: Doc: one read-write prod account, prompt-only guard; repo summary: raw subprocess, no allowlist, no sandbox, no audit log; eval is 12 scripted alerts run once.

DELIVERABLE: Critical: injection through linked pages can reach destructive SQL and shell; the 'never destructive' system prompt is a request, not enforcement, so move to least-privilege read-only credentials, sandbox, command allowlist and human approval for writes. Replace the 12 single-run scenarios with repeated runs. Praise: stating the destructive-command rule at all shows risk awareness.
BOUNDARY: Doc plus summary; implementation unverified and no production access reviewed.
EVIDENCE: Shared prod-writing service account, unrestricted subprocess, no audit trail, and 12 scenarios run once each.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement; the system prompt forbids destructive commands so risk is acceptable; add more test alerts.
BOUNDARY: Doc and summary.
EVIDENCE: Service account and 12 alerts.
